newsitem.title: CANADA: Bovar says investigating mechanical fault.
newsitem.headline: Bovar says investigating mechanical fault.

text.p: Bovar Inc said on Wednesday that chemicals released after the mechanical failure of a high temperature expansion joint in the transformer furnace flue gas duct at its Swan Hills Treatment Center did not appear to pose a threat to employees or the public.
The transformer furnace was shut down for the completion of investigations after the incident.
Bovar said it began investigating right after the incident on October 16 and that test results indicated that Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), dioxins and furans were released into the environment.

Test results indicated that the release did not pose a significant threat to employee or public health. Bovar received technical information relating to the investigation last weekend. Additional testing was under way to verify the results and to assess potential environmental impact.
Routine ambient air monitoring results at the plant site indicated a maximum 24-hour PCB concentration of 3.6 micrograms per cubic meter adjacent to the transformer furnace.
That corresponded to about 11 micrograms per cubic meter over the estimated eight-hour duration of the incident.
In comparison, the Alberta eight-hour occupational exposure limit for PCBs was 500 micrograms per cubic meter, Bovar said.
